parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a strongly protective division with a hostile federal layer the state cannot displace. Documented federal exposures are universal or near-universal for an outed visitor: passport/marker restrictions with blocked issues, consular instructions to refuse cases where documents cast doubt on sex (with fraud-bar consideration), a bar from federally funded single-sex facilities, and hostile federal custody practices (hormone removal, immigration-detention abuse). At division level the law runs protective — public-accommodations and hate-crime coverage since 1993, shield law, open ID rules, no documented facility ban, top-tier 2026 risk rating — but enforcement data is absent and birth-sex custody placement is documented. No organised targeting or documented visitor violence. Universal federal exposures without a shown working remedy keep this in elevated risk, mid-band.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal: Feb 2025 elimination of X markers for new issues, markers fixed to sex assigned at birth, passport issues blocked/confiscated; consular cable directs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and referral for possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; multiple governments issued travel advisories for trans visitors.
entry_documents.protection: Division-level ID rules are open (licence X marker, no-document marker change, birth-certificate change without surgery) but these govern resident documents, not the traveller's foreign passport. A legal-aid FAQ and pending litigation offer partial, unproven relief.
entry_documents.interaction: Border and passport control are federal; the division's open ID regime cannot offset entry refusal, additional-evidence demands, or a fraud finding at the federal desk.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policy (forced short hair, hormone removal, substitute psychiatric drugs) from 2026; trans immigration detainees report forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse. Division custody places by birth sex: 2012 case held in men's facility throughout, attacked in custody.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; the division's attacker in the 2012 case was prosecuted and jailed, and a petition restored correct hormones. Division abolished the trans panic defence in 2024.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A detained visitor falls into federal or division custody regardless of the division's equality laws; a document discrepancy can escalate from entry refusal into detention where birth-sex placement applies.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity — applying nationwide, including within this protective division. Nationally, 4 units criminalise trans bathroom use in certain circumstances and a trans student was arrested and held in a men's ward in 2025.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The division has no documented facility ban and sits in the July 2026 map's most-protective tier; division anti-discrimination law covers public accommodations since 1993. Roughly 29 units plus the capital district also lack bans.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The federal facility bar operates inside the division, so state-level acceptance does not shield a visitor in federal buildings; the trespass statute cited applies only in its own unit.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders frame minor gender-affirming care as 'mutilation', direct investigations of schools, and DOJ subpoenaed 'over 20' hospitals for under-19 patient records including names and notes; proposed rules would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans patients.
care_services.protection: Division shield law declares gender-affirming care against public policy for out-of-state enforcement, bars enforcing out-of-state subpoenas, warrants and extradition, and blocks out-of-state custody-removal orders; coverage written into division policy; conversion therapy banned for minors and vulnerable adults since 2023.
care_services.interaction: Families travelling to the division for care are shielded from other units' process, but federal investigations, subpoenas and any federal custody encounter remain outside the shield's documented reach.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal executive orders use 'chemical and surgical mutilation' and 'gender ideology'; the May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; Dec 2025 rewards memo invokes 'radical gender ideology' among extreme viewpoints. Public opinion: 66% back ASAB-only document listing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Division repealed residual 'does not condone homosexuality' language in 2023, added gender-identity hate-crime penalties in 1993, and abolished the trans panic defence in 2024; the rewards memo does not make ideology a reward criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing raises the severity of any stop, dispute or investigation; division law moderates the local response but cannot instruct federal agents.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal order directs law enforcement to criminally prosecute teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition and revokes funding; federal care restrictions and hospital-record subpoenas reach minors; the division's own athlete policy is in litigation.
minors_guardians.protection: Division shield law blocks out-of-state custody-removal orders over gender-affirming care and protects families travelling for treatment; conversion therapy banned; LGBTQ family formation recognised in practice.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a minor is shielded at division level from other units' process, but entry screening, federal facility rules and federal custody apply to the whole family unit.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific figure on violence against trans residents or visitors exists in the record. National data show bias against sexual orientation at one-seventh to one-fifth of single-bias hate incidents; only 23 units cover gender identity in bias-crime statutes (federal coverage fills part of this gap).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division hate-crime law has covered gender identity since 1993 with additional penalties; employment and public-accommodation discrimination barred since 1993; federal hate-crime statute applies.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Unknown local violence rate means the state's protections rest on paper plus statute; the absence of state-specific incident data is not evidence of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Enforcement data for division hate-crime and non-discrimination provisions is absent; the shield law has no decided applying cases; current division custody placement beyond the dated 2012 case is undocumented; some federal orders are enjoined while others (passport rules) are in force, so exposure varies by travel date.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Pending litigation, a legal-aid passport-rules FAQ, and a July 2026 independent assessment placing the division in its most-protective tier; several federal orders blocked or enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation volatility means the operative federal rule at travel time is uncertain; division remedies cannot reach federal border, facility or custody decisions.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has birth-sex toilets in all public buildings with courts upholding exclusion and no border element. This dossier's federal facility bar is narrower (federally funded facilities only) and the division adds genuine protections, but it adds heavier features 0.35-A lacks: entry refusal with possible lifetime fraud bar, foreign travel advisories, and federal custody hormone removal. Worse on border and custody, better on division facilities and services — so slightly above.

Closest match. 0.45-A: national birth-sex bathroom rule in publicly funded buildings upheld, passports accepted, no criminalisation, no organised arrests. Here the facility rule is federal-level, passports are actively scrutinised with refusal and fraud-referral instructions, and custody carries conversion-style policies — heavier. But the division supplies documented, long-standing public-accommodation and hate-crime protections absent from 0.45-A. Net roughly level, marginally above.

0.65-D has functioning courts convicting an attacker, only minority service refusals, patchy but real remedies, no universal facility ban and no border friction, with detention placement unknown. This dossier is materially lower: it documents federal universal facility exclusion, border refusal instructions and severe federal custody practice — tier-1 and tier-2 exposures 0.65-D lacks — which division-level protections cannot offset.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system with two layers pulling opposite ways. The division offers unusually strong, long-dated machinery: public-accommodations and gender-identity hate-crime coverage since 1993, a 2023 shield law protecting travelling families, open identity documents, a conversion-therapy ban, abolished trans panic defence, no documented facility ban, and a July 2026 top-tier protective rating. The federal layer, however, imposes exposures every outed visitor carries: document scrutiny at entry with refusal and fraud-bar referral, exclusion from federally funded single-sex facilities operating inside this division, hostile official framing, and — if detained — birth-sex custody plus federal conversion-style policies and documented immigration-detention abuse. Enforcement data for the division's protections is missing, and its one custody record shows birth-sex placement. Because tier-1 federal exposures lack a shown working remedy and state protections cannot reach the border, cells or federal buildings, the score sits mid-elevated-risk rather than in reduced risk; litigation volatility and the absence of division violence data keep it below the upper half of that band.
